3.3.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation establishes a specific service unit: Pasal 11(1) “Pemerintah Daerah membentuk PPT” (Pusat Pelayanan Terpadu / Integrated Service Center) to provide protection/services, and Pasal 1 angka 15 defines PPT as a comprehensive service unit providing information services, assistance, counseling, medical services, and safe house via referral. While the text does not explicitly say “hotline,” it does create a designated integrated service center that would function as a reporting/complaint intake point in practice, and Pasal 5 huruf g guarantees “penanganan pengaduan” (complaint handling). The retrieved candidates included the PPT definition ([3.3-3], item 15) and complaint-handling right ([3.3-7]), so a “Yes” is supportable from the document. Thus the golden label “Yes” is consistent, and the judge’s “No” was overly strict in requiring an explicit hotline/complaint desk label despite a designated service center being defined.

5.5.rationale: The original Indonesian text does not mention “organisasi internasional” or international bodies in the cooperation/partnership provisions. Pasal 21(2) lists cooperation partners: Pemerintah Pusat, Pemerintah Provinsi, Pemerintah Kabupaten/Kota lain, Perguruan Tinggi, Lembaga Sosial dan Keagamaan, LSM, dan/atau Media—these are domestic categories. Pasal 22 discusses partnership with “dunia usaha” (business sector) without international reference. Although Pasal 26 allows funding sources including “bantuan luar negeri yang tidak mengikat” (non-binding foreign aid), that is not engagement with international organizations per se. The judge’s “No” aligns with the Indonesian text and the retrieved passages. Thus the golden label “Yes” likely reflects a coding error or an overly broad interpretation equating foreign aid with international-organization engagement.

5.6.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly lists "Media" as one of the entities with which the Regional Government may conduct cooperation.
